`# Service Accounts\\n${serviceAccountLines.join('\\n')}\\n\\n# Edge Device Accounts\\n`\n        : '# Edge Device Accounts\\n';\n\n      const deviceEntries: string[] = [];\n      for (const [user, hash] of entries) {\n        if (!this.serviceAccounts.has(user)) {\n          deviceEntries.push(`${user}:${hash}`);\n        }\n      }\n\n      const newContent = header + serviceSection + deviceEntries.join('\\n') + '\\n';\n\n      // Atomic write: temp file → fsync → rename (restrictive permissions)\n      const tmpPath = this.passwordFilePath + '.tmp';\n      await fs.writeFile(tmpPath, newContent, { encoding: 'utf-8', mode: 0o600 });\n      const fileHandle = await fs.open(tmpPath, 'r');\n      await fileHandle.datasync();\n      await fileHandle.close();\n      await fs.rename(tmpPath, this.passwordFilePath);\n\n      this.logger.log(`Added MQTT credentials for device: ${username}`);\n      await this.reloadMosquitto();\n      return true;\n    } catch (error) {\n      this.logger.error(`Failed to add MQTT credentials for ${username}:`, error);\n      return false;\n    }\n  }\n\n  private async _removeDeviceCredentialsFile(username: string): Promise<boolean> {\n    if (!this.fileAuthEnabled) return true;\n\n    try {\n      let content = await fs.readFile(this.passwordFilePath, 'utf-8');\n      const lines = content.split('\\n');\n\n      const filteredLines = lines.filter((line) => {\n        if (!line.trim() || line.startsWith('#')) return true;\n        const colonIndex = line.indexOf(':');\n        return colonIndex > 0 ? line.substring(0, colonIndex) !== username : true;\n      });\n\n      content = filteredLines.join('\\n');\n\n      const tmpPath = this.passwordFilePath + '.tmp';\n      await fs.writeFile(tmpPath, content, { encoding: 'utf-8', mode: 0o600 });\n      const fileHandle = await fs.open(tmpPath, 'r');\n      await fileHandle.datasync();\n      await fileHandle.close();\n      await fs.rename(tmpPath, this.passwordFilePath);\n\n      this.logger.log(`Removed MQTT credentials for device: ${username}`);\n      await this.reloadMosquitto();\n      return true;\n    } catch (error) {\n      this.logger.error(`Failed to remove MQTT credentials for ${username}:`, error);\n      return false;\n    }\n  }\n\n  private async reloadMosquitto(): Promise<boolean> {\n    try {\n      try {\n        // Use execFile with explicit args to avoid shell injection\n        await execFileAsync('mosquitto_pid_reload', [], { timeout: 5000 }).catch(async () => {\n          // Fallback: use pkill to send SIGHUP without shell interpolation\n          await execFileAsync('pkill', ['-HUP', 'mosquitto'], { timeout: 5000 });\n        });\n        this.logger.log('Mosquitto reload signal sent');\n      } catch {\n        try {\n          // Docker fallback: use execFile with explicit args (no shell)\n          await execFileAsync('docker', ['exec', 'mosquitto', 'kill', '-HUP', '1'], { timeout: 5000 });\n          this.logger.log('Mosquitto reload signal sent via Docker');\n        } catch {\n          this.logger.warn('Could not reload Mosquitto - may need manual restart');\n        }\n      }\n      return true;\n    } catch (error) {\n      this.logger.warn(`Mosquitto reload failed: ${error instanceof Error ? Walk each argument back to its origin. Its hazard model is taint: if an attacker can influence the argument, they can steer a read or write outside the intended path (traversal, clobbering a neighbouring file, following a planted link). The whole value of the rule rests on that source-to-sink chain existing.\\n\\nWHAT THE CODE ACTUALLY DOES. A judge must separate that syntactic truth from the security claim; conflating them is how a lint hit gets mistaken for a vulnerability.\\n\\nTHE TAINT TRACE (the step that decides the verdict). Walk each argument back to its origin. (1) `this.passwordFilePath` is declared `private readonly` at line 44 and written exactly once, in the constructor at line 93, from `configService.get<string>('MOSQUITTO_PASSWORD_FILE', ...)` with a string-literal fallback at line 95 — a deployment environment value resolved at process start, which SPEC L1 treats as trusted config, not request data. (2) `tmpPath` at line 784 is that same field plus the literal `'.tmp'`, so it inherits the field's provenance and adds nothing. (3) The one caller-supplied value in the enclosing method, `username` (line 769, reached from the public `removeDeviceCredentials` at line 660 through line 669), is used to filter lines of the file's CONTENT at line 779 and is never concatenated into either path. No request-bound input reaches either filename, so the chain the rule depends on is absent and the HIGH severity has nothing behind it.\\n\\nWHY THIS MATTERS DOWNSTREAM, AND WHAT BREAKS IF THE STEP IS SKIPPED. Accepting this as a true positive teaches the feedback store that config-sourced paths are defects. Every atomic-write sequence in the repository uses this same shape, so the adapter's precision drops, real taint-carrying `fs` hits get buried in a wash of identical noise, and the next genuine traversal bug arrives in a queue operators have learned to skim. The affected downstream surface is the consensus arbiter and the lint-rules adapter's calibration, not sensor-service runtime.\\n\\nWHERE MY CONFIDENCE IS LIMITED. The admissible evidence is this single file, which lets me prove there is no in-file writer of the field; what I cannot read here is whether a bootstrap config layer populates `MOSQUITTO_PASSWORD_FILE` from somewhere unexpected. The field being `readonly` and constructor-assigned confines any such source to process startup rather than a request, which bounds that gap but does not erase it — hence 0.88 rather than higher.\\n\\nTHE ROOT-CAUSE-SHAPED FIX, IF THE OPERATOR WANTS THE RULE SILENCED HONESTLY. Do not blanket-disable the rule at the callsite; that hides the class instead of answering it. Resolve the config value once at construction through a validated path helper — `path.resolve` plus a containment assertion against an allowed base directory, returning a branded path type that the write/open/rename calls accept — so the constraint on the filename is structural (Tier 1) rather than argued in a comment.
